chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whose wife had gone over to the disbelievers, and Allah, the Exalted, had said in His Book: 'And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you are then victorious, give those whose wives have gone what they spent.' I asked: 'What is the meaning of 'retribution' (uqubah) here?'

He said: 'That the one whose wife went should take retribution upon another woman, meaning he marries her in succession. So when he marries another woman besides her, then it is upon the Imam to give him her dowry, which is the dowry of his wife who went.'
I said: 'How is it that the believers repay her husband without any action of their own in her going, and the believers must repay her husband what they spent on her from what the believers acquire?'

He said: 'The Imam repays him whether they acquired from the disbelievers or did not acquire, because it is upon the Imam to authorize a group from under his hand. And if the distribution arrives, he may fill every deputyship that replaces him before the distribution. And if something remains after that, he distributes it among them. And if nothing remains for them, then there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.بِعَقِبٍ: In succession or as a substitute

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of uqabah (retribution) for a husband whose wife migrates to the disbelievers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that 'retribution' (uqabah) refers to the Imam providing a substitute wife to the husband whose spouse migrated to the disbelievers, with her dowry funded from the Imam's treasury or war booty. It establishes the Imam's discretionary authority to allocate resources for this compensation even before the final distribution of spoils, ensuring the husband's rights are upheld regardless of actual wealth acquisition.
